course_name_original: Sistemas de Información en la Ingeniería

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of database and design, implement and optimize databases.
Know the functionality and characteristics of database management systems.
Determine the needs related to information systems.
Know and select data exchange standards.
Understand the basic elements of programming, structured programming, and object-oriented programming.
Develop programs using standard market libraries.
Understand the problems in integrating information systems.
Determine the selection criteria for tools and components for information system integration.

syllabus_topics: Relational databases. Design and optimization. Information retrieval
Advanced information systems. Data warehouses and multidimensional modeling
Creation, manipulation and querying of databases
Basic development of graphical interfaces for data access
teaching_methods: Individual activities on the Virtual Campus

assessment_methods.method: Project (Theoretical Task 1: Building an E/R diagram)
Project (Theoretical Task 2: Converting an E/R diagram to tables)
Project (Practical Task 3: Creating, modifying, deleting tables, data manipulation, and SQL queries)
Project (Practical Task 4: Procedures, functions, packages, and PL/SQL triggers)
In-person exam related to project tasks

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.75 * (0.25 * T1 + 0.1 * T2 + 0.25 * T3 + 0.3 * T4 + 0.1 * T5) + 0.25 * EX. To pass, each task score (T1-T5) and the exam score (EX) must be 50 points or higher out of 100. If any score is below 50, the final grade will be the minimum of 4.0 out of 10 and the weighted average. For the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of two in-person tests (theoretical and practical) with similar weighting, and each section (A1-A5) must score 50 points or higher out of 100. Non-submitted activities count as zero; if their total weight exceeds 50%, the final grade will be 'not presented'.
